# Ethereum L1 — Colosseum resource index

Every link below is copied verbatim from Colosseum's published corpus, including its curator caveats.

### Start here

**Core resources**

- [Ethereum developer documentation](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/)
  - Use the canonical map of accounts, transactions, the EVM, smart contracts, clients, and application frameworks.
- [SpeedRunEthereum](https://speedrunethereum.com/)
  - Learn by shipping guided contracts and interfaces, starting with tokenization and progressing to DeFi, oracles, and security challenges.
- [Scaffold-ETH 2 installation](https://docs.scaffoldeth.io/quick-start/installation)
  - Generate a full-stack Ethereum app with wallet UI, contract hooks, a local chain, and a choice of Hardhat or Foundry.
- [Foundry getting started](https://www.getfoundry.sh/introduction/getting-started)
  - Build, test, debug, deploy, verify, query, and fork contracts with Forge, Cast, Anvil, and Chisel.
- [Hardhat 3 getting started](https://hardhat.org/docs/getting-started)
  - Choose the TypeScript-oriented contract workflow with Solidity and TypeScript tests, viem integration, plugins, and Ignition deployments.

### Ethereum L1 context

**Execution and networks**

- [Ethereum networks and testnets](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/networks/)
  - Use Sepolia for application testing, reserve Hoodi for validator and protocol work, and avoid deprecated testnets.
- [Ethereum gas and fees](https://ethereum.org/developers/docs/gas/)
  - Budget L1 transactions by understanding gas used, base and priority fees, refunds, failed execution, and block demand.

### Contracts and clients

**Contract components**

- [OpenZeppelin Contracts 5.x](https://docs.openzeppelin.com/contracts/5.x)
  - Install audited implementations for tokens, access control, signatures, governance, utilities, and upgrade patterns instead of copying snippets.

**TypeScript clients**

- [viem getting started](https://viem.sh/docs/getting-started)
  - Create typed public and wallet clients for Ethereum RPC reads, writes, signatures, logs, and contract calls.
- [wagmi React getting started](https://wagmi.sh/react/getting-started)
  - Add wallet connections and reactive Ethereum state to React through viem-backed hooks and TanStack Query.

### Smart accounts

**Account abstraction**

- [ERC-4337 documentation](https://docs.erc4337.io/)
  - Understand UserOperations, EntryPoint, bundlers, paymasters, smart accounts, and the extra infrastructure behind account abstraction.
- [Safe Protocol Kit](https://docs.safe.global/sdk/protocol-kit)
  - Create, configure, sign, and execute transactions from Safe smart accounts with a maintained TypeScript SDK.

### Secure the contract workflow

**Security basics**

- [Solidity security considerations](https://docs.soliditylang.org/en/latest/security-considerations.html)
  - Review reentrancy, authorization, randomness, loops, Ether transfer, proxies, compiler bugs, and other contract-level hazards.
- [Foundry fork testing](https://www.getfoundry.sh/guides/fork-testing)
  - Test integrations against pinned Ethereum mainnet state with account impersonation, time changes, token balances, and reproducible fork configuration.

**Analysis and practice**

- [Slither](https://github.com/crytic/slither#readme)
  - Run static detectors and review printers over a Hardhat or Foundry project and export findings for CI or SARIF tooling.
- [Ethernaut](https://ethernaut.openzeppelin.com/)
  - Practice finding and exploiting Solidity mistakes in a maintained EVM wargame before handling real assets.

### Index contract events

**Event indexers**

- [Ponder get started](https://ponder.sh/docs/get-started)
  - Write a TypeScript event indexer that stores Ethereum data in Postgres and exposes GraphQL, SQL over HTTP, or direct SQL.
- [The Graph subgraph quick start](https://thegraph.com/docs/en/subgraphs/quick-start/)
  - Generate a subgraph from a deployed contract, test it in Studio, and publish it to The Graph Network when public decentralized indexing matters.
